title: All Saints’ Cathedral, Prayagraj - The “Patthar Girja” of Uttar Pradesh
content:
All Saints’ Cathedral, Prayagraj

All Saints’ Cathedral, popularly known as Patthar Girja, is one of the most beautiful and historic churches in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad). Located in the heart of the city near Thornhill Road, this cathedral is a remarkable example of Gothic Revival architecture and a peaceful place for visitors seeking history, architecture, and calm surroundings.

History of All Saints’ Cathedral

All Saints’ Cathedral was built during the British colonial period. The foundation stone was laid in 1871, and the cathedral was completed in 1887. It was designed by Sir William Emerson, the same architect who designed the famous Victoria Memorial in Kolkata. The church was built to serve the Anglican community of Allahabad, which was an important administrative center during British rule.

Architectural Beauty

The cathedral is made entirely of light-colored stone, which is why locals call it Patthar Girja. Its design reflects classic English Gothic architecture, featuring:

Tall pointed arches

High vaulted ceilings

Beautiful stained-glass windows

Elegant stone carvings

A majestic bell tower

The interior is equally impressive, with sunlight filtering through stained glass, creating a calm and spiritual atmosphere.

Religious and Cultural Importance

All Saints’ Cathedral is an active place of worship and holds regular Sunday prayers, Christmas services, and special ceremonies. It also stands as an important cultural landmark, reminding visitors of Prayagraj’s colonial past and religious diversity.

Peaceful Ambience

Surrounded by greenery and away from heavy traffic noise, the cathedral offers a quiet and serene environment. Many visitors come not only for prayers but also to admire the architecture and enjoy moments of peace.

Visitor Information

  • Location: Thornhill Road, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh
  • Best time to visit: Morning hours or during Christmas celebrations
  • Entry fee: Free
  • Photography: Allowed (avoid during prayer time)

Nearby Places to Visit

  • Allahabad High Court
  • Khusro Bagh
  • Anand Bhavan
  • Alfred Park (Chandrashekhar Azad Park)

Conclusion

All Saints’ Cathedral is more than just a church-it is a symbol of Prayagraj’s rich historical and architectural heritage. Whether you are a history lover, architecture enthusiast, or a traveler seeking calm, this magnificent cathedral deserves a place on your travel list.
excerpt: All Saints’ Cathedral, also known as Patthar Girja, is a stunning Gothic-style church built during British rule in Prayagraj. Designed by Sir William Emerson, it is admired for its stone structure and beautiful stained-glass windows. The cathedral is a peaceful heritage site and an important religious landmark of the city.

faqs.question: Why is All Saints’ Cathedral called Patthar Girja?
faqs.answer: It is called Patthar Girja because the entire structure is made of stone.

faqs.question: Who designed All Saints’ Cathedral in Prayagraj?
faqs.answer: The cathedral was designed by Sir William Emerson, the architect of Victoria Memorial, Kolkata.

faqs.question: Is All Saints’ Cathedral open to visitors?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is open to visitors and worshippers. Entry is free.

faqs.question: Where is All Saints’ Cathedral located?
faqs.answer: It is located on Thornhill Road, near the Allahabad High Court in Prayagraj.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit All Saints’ Cathedral?
faqs.answer: Morning hours and festive occasions like Christmas are the best times to visit.
